findings.issue: REQ-002's edge cases prescribe TWO DIFFERENT degrade behaviors: a `verify-error` (RPC infra failure) gets a narrate-only trace.jsonl line, while an `unconfirmed` signature (a definitive on-chain fact) is spec'd to have its reason "logged to stderr only" (not necessarily to trace.jsonl). The FIND-007 fix collapses BOTH (plus bad-args/no-delta) into the SAME trace.jsonl `sol-verify-failed` line, so an `unconfirmed` status now also gets a durable trace.jsonl entry beyond the spec's literal wording for that sub-case. This does not violate any money-safety invariant (earn-ledger.jsonl is untouched either way, and no proof obligation tests trace.jsonl-absence for the unconfirmed case) -- it is a stricter/more-auditable behavior than literally specified, not a functional regression. Non-blocking.

The CLI-entrypoint self-invocation guard uses `import.meta.url.endsWith(process.argv[1].split("/").pop())` (a basename-suffix match), whereas every other new/touched module in this feature (parse-pass.mjs:29, resolve-identity.mjs:143, record.mjs:34) uses the stronger, standard `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` idiom. In every ACTUAL call site in this feature (run.sh invokes it via an absolute path) the weaker check is functionally correct and does not misfire during `node --test` imports (verified: process.argv[1] during test runs is the test file's own path, whose basename never equals 'record-swap.mjs'). This is a cosmetic inconsistency, not a demonstrated functional defect. Non-blocking.

The behavioral-spec's Acceptance Criteria for PROP-014(c) (Franklin-shaped fixture) says the fixture's Solana secret should be "readable via the SAME legacy .solana-session path the real CLI's own wallet setup reads." The actual test fixture instead writes `.automaton/solana.json` under the `.blockrun`-shaped fixture home, so BOTH the own-ANICCA_HOME derivation and the forced-.blockrun derivation resolve via resolveSolanaSecret's 2nd-priority (ANICCA_HOME-file) branch rather than its 3rd-priority (legacy .solana-session) branch -- the identity-match guard's core equality-check logic is still genuinely proven (same effectiveHome -> same file -> same address, for two separately-invoked node processes), but the SPECIFIC legacy-path branch is not exercised at this full-integration level. That branch IS separately covered at the unit level (runtime/loop/__tests__/resolve-identity.test.mjs:158-165, unmodified/pre-existing), so the underlying resolution logic is not actually unproven -- only the AC's literal fixture-shape wording is not matched. Non-blocking.
